newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends mixed, sells off near close.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends mixed, sells off near close.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed mixed with early gains eroded in late dealings by local and commission house selling, traders said.
Traders said Merrill Lynch Futures, Prudential Securities, Cargill Inc and Fimat Futures keyed a selloff near the close.
Wheat was underpinned by a strong recovery in soybeans and on signals the wheat market was oversold and due for a bounce.
"The bullish consensus was down to 12 which is very low and wheat got a little help from other markets. Wheat was very oversold," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Wheat tumbled to new contract lows Tuesday in response of USDA's weekly crop ratings late Monday which showed the U.S. winter crop in mostly good to excellent condition.
Fundamentals were little changed with the growing supply of wheat worldwide and competitive prices from export competitors limiting rallies.
December wheat's daily relative strength index (RSI) was at 27 points at the close. The market considers an RSI of 30 or less as oversold but traders said the long-term indicators remain bearish.
Wheat closed 2-1/2 cents per bushel higher to 1-1/2 lower, with December up 3/4 at $3.69-1/2.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 15,000 contracts, down from 19,949 Tuesday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options, Term Commodities bought 800 March $3.70 calls at 12-1/2 to 13-1/2 cents and O'Connor and Co bought 300 July $3.80 calls at 8-1/2 to 8-3/4 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 8,000 contracts, up from 6,619 Tuesday.
